description: Instance-wide settings for a hardened GitLab self-managed instance. Both checkers read this file. Edit expect values to match your own policy.

checks.why: Administrators must re-authenticate before using admin rights, and API tokens need the admin_mode scope.
Web sessions last at most 8 hours (value in minutes). The default is a week.
The session lifetime counts from sign-in, so activity cannot keep a session alive indefinitely.
Remember me keeps users signed in beyond the session lifetime.
Users get an email when someone signs in to their account from an unknown IP address.
Anyone who can reach the sign-in page can register an account while this is on.
A safety net if sign-up is turned back on: new accounts wait for an administrator.
Users must confirm their email address before they can sign in.
GitLab deactivates accounts that have not been used, so leavers missed by the joiners and leavers process lose access.
Days of inactivity before deactivation.
Only administrators create top-level groups, so every group sits under a governed parent.
Guests cannot create projects.
New users get no personal projects, so code lives in groups the organisation controls. The default is 100,000.
New projects start private.
New groups start private.
New snippets start private.
Only administrators can make a project, group or snippet public.
Personal, project and group access tokens must have an expiry date.
Service account tokens must have an expiry date. On Free GitLab always requires one; on Premium and Ultimate this setting decides.
Caps token lifetime in days. Below Ultimate GitLab saves this value but does not enforce it.
Users cannot register their own OAuth applications.
Administrators cannot authorise untrusted OAuth applications that ask for scopes such as api, read_repository or sudo.
Webhooks and integrations cannot reach the internal network, which limits server-side request forgery.
System hooks cannot reach the internal network.
Stops a hostname that resolves to a public address at check time from resolving to an internal one at request time.
Exports by administrators are recorded in the audit log and notify project members.
Users sign in through the organisation's identity provider, not a GitLab password. Only set this once SSO works.
Git over HTTPS uses tokens, not the account password.
Applies to GitLab password sign-in. Users who sign in through SSO get MFA from the identity provider.
Hours a user can delay setting up two-factor authentication.
Administrators must use two-factor authentication.
